page.title: Cleft Sentences and Emphasis
page.subtitle_html: Cleft Sentences and Emphasis - C1 focus structures with it-clefts, what-clefts, and contrastive emphasis.
page.subtitle_text: C1 focus structures with it-clefts, what-clefts, and contrastive emphasis.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Cleft Sentences and Emphasis: C1 anchors for highlighting people, things, places, reasons, and actions with cleft patterns.","rules":[{"label":"It-cleft","text":"Use it is / was + focused element + that / who clause.","example":"It was Anna who solved the problem."},{"label":"What-cleft","text":"Use what + clause + be + focused element to emphasize an action, need, or result.","example":"What we need is a clearer plan."},{"label":"Question focus","text":"Use cleft question patterns to make the focus explicit.","example":"When was it that the company changed the policy?"}]}

blocks.heading: C1 focus
blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder C1 cleft sentences lesson package.

page.title: Complex Noun Phrases
page.subtitle_html: Complex Noun Phrases - C2 noun groups with dense premodification, postmodification, apposition, and embedded clauses.
page.subtitle_text: C2 noun groups with dense premodification, postmodification, apposition, and embedded clauses.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Complex noun phrases: compact C2 anchors for dense noun groups in formal and academic English.","rules":[{"label":"Premodification","text":"Build meaning before the head noun with adjectives, nouns, and participles.","example":"The sharp increase in energy prices affected small businesses."},{"label":"Postmodification","text":"Add precision after the head noun with prepositional phrases, infinitives, and clauses.","example":"The question of how to fund the programme remains unresolved."},{"label":"Information density","text":"Use complex noun phrases to package abstract ideas without creating long chains of finite clauses.","example":"The rapid expansion of urban infrastructure created new risks."}]}

blocks.heading: C2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on complex noun phrases.

page.title: Ellipsis Substitution And Reference
page.subtitle_html: Ellipsis Substitution And Reference - C2 cohesion through so, not, do so, one/ones, such, former/latter, and this/that reference.
page.subtitle_text: C2 cohesion through so, not, do so, one/ones, such, former/latter, and this/that reference.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Ellipsis, substitution and reference: compact C2 anchors for avoiding repetition while keeping reference clear.","rules":[{"label":"So and not","text":"Use so or not to replace a whole previous idea when the reference is unambiguous.","example":"The plan may work, and I hope so."},{"label":"Do so and one/ones","text":"Use do so for repeated actions, and one/ones for repeated countable nouns.","example":"They promised to revise the draft and did so promptly."},{"label":"Former, latter and reference","text":"Use the former, the latter, this, and that to connect ideas across sentences or clauses.","example":"The former is cheaper; the latter is more reliable."}]}

blocks.heading: C2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on cohesive substitution and reference.
